title: Breast Lift Scars: Where They Are and How They Fade
meta_description: Where breast lift scars sit for each type of lift, how they change over the first year, and what the evidence says about sunscreen, silicone and creams.
excerpt: Every breast lift leaves a scar. Where it sits depends on how much lift you need, and most of the fading happens in the first year. Here is what to expect month by month, what helps, and what doesn't have good evidence behind it.
quick_answer:
Do breast lift scars go away?

No, but they fade. Cleveland Clinic says breast lift scars are permanent but fade a lot, most of it in about 1 year. The Aesthetic Society says incisions stay red or pink for many months. Where they sit depends on the lift: around the areola, down to the breast crease, and sometimes along the crease.

notes: Full rewrite of the live January post from the approved 3 Nov brief (posts.md section 3 + bl.md 2.5). Removed: '80% fear', '94%' (Swanson 2013, mixed sample), the $6K-$12K line was not in this post's live text; removed 12-24 months, 'redness peaks at 6-8 weeks', massage counts, silicone 12+ hours as advice, the 1.3% misquote, the humidity and nutrition sections (unsourced), the Miami climate section, financing lender names, ABCS link, AAAASF, phone, the quiz link. Live FAQs kept in new form: how long to fade, least noticeable scar, do they fade completely, when to start treatment, the beach. Fact-check pass 3 Nov: the bar on '12 to 18 months' was lifted where a named source says it, so Horton's figure is stated as hers (the coordinator's fix); the facts file's 'about 1 year' stays Cleveland Clinic's. di Summa's 'minor complications' caveat is dropped because the abstract read doesn't say it. Maman's 5-10 lb lifting limit is left out (the cluster states no weight limit). No Alluring revision policy, scar protocol or photos are stated (owner questions). Consented dated scar photos at 1, 3 and 12 months would still be the SERP gap, if the practice has them. The Aesthetic Society's own heading for its least common option uses a word the lint bans; the post quotes only 'require incisions of some sort'.
